concepts.title: Values, variables and basic types
concepts.objective: Understand variables, basic types (int, float, str, bool), and assignments.

worked_example.title: Variable assignment and type inspection
worked_example.code:
x = 42
y = 3.14
name = 'Forge'
is_active = True
print(type(x), type(y), type(name), type(is_active))
worked_example.explanation: Variables store references to values. Types are assigned dynamically at runtime.

concepts.title: Arithmetic expressions and precedence
concepts.objective: Evaluate arithmetic expressions using order of operations, floor division and modulo.

worked_example.title: Floor division and precedence
worked_example.code:
total = 10 + 2 * 5
quotient = 17 // 3
remainder = 17 % 3
print(total, quotient, remainder)
worked_example.explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition. // performs floor division, % gives remainder.

concepts.title: Comparisons and Boolean branching
concepts.objective: Use relational operators (==, !=, <, >) and if/elif/else statements.

worked_example.title: Branching with if/else
worked_example.explanation: Branches are evaluated from top to bottom; the first true condition executes its block.

concepts.title: Modulo and compound conditions
concepts.objective: Combine conditions using and, or, not, and modulo checks.

worked_example.title: Compound conditions
worked_example.code:
n = 15
is_fizzbuzz = (n % 3 == 0) and (n % 5 == 0)
print('Divisible by 3 and 5:', is_fizzbuzz)
worked_example.explanation: The and operator requires both operands to be truthy.

concepts.title: For loops and range iteration
concepts.objective: Iterate using for loops over ranges and collections, updating accumulators.

worked_example.title: Accumulation over range
worked_example.code:
total = 0
for i in range(1, 6):
    total += i
print('Sum 1 to 5:', total)
worked_example.explanation: range(start, stop) generates integers from start up to stop - 1.

concepts.title: Loop tracing and finding extremes
concepts.objective: Track loop state across iterations and identify minimums or maximums.

worked_example.title: Tracing maximum value
worked_example.explanation: Comparing each item against the running maximum finds the peak in one pass.

concepts.title: String indexing and transformations
concepts.objective: Index characters, slice substrings, and check character properties.

worked_example.title: Reversing and indexing strings
worked_example.code:
word = 'level'
is_palindrome = (word == word[::-1])
print(word, 'palindrome?', is_palindrome)
worked_example.explanation: Slice `[::-1]` produces the reversed string in Python.

concepts.title: Lists, sets, and frequency tracking
concepts.objective: Use lists, sets for uniqueness, and dictionaries for frequency counts.

worked_example.title: Deduplicating while counting
worked_example.code:
items = ['apple', 'banana', 'apple', 'orange']
unique = set(items)
print('Unique items:', sorted(unique))
worked_example.explanation: Sets drop duplicate entries in O(1) average lookup time.

concepts.title: Tables, rows and scalar projection
concepts.objective: Understand relational tables, data types, and simple SELECT expressions.

worked_example.title: Scalar SELECT
worked_example.code: SELECT 100 AS base_score, 'Active' AS status;
worked_example.explanation: SELECT computes and labels output columns.

concepts.title: Reading columns and table structure
concepts.objective: Project specific columns from an existing table.

worked_example.title: Column projection
worked_example.code: SELECT first_name, email FROM employees;
worked_example.explanation: Selecting specific columns reduces unnecessary data transfer.

concepts.title: Filtering rows with WHERE
concepts.objective: Filter rows using comparison operators, AND, OR, and string matches.

worked_example.title: Row filtering with predicates
worked_example.code: SELECT id, product_name FROM products WHERE price > 50 AND in_stock = true;
worked_example.explanation: Only rows satisfying all WHERE predicates are returned.

concepts.title: Handling missing data (NULL)
concepts.objective: Distinguish NULL from empty values and use IS NULL and COALESCE.

worked_example.title: COALESCE fallback for NULL
worked_example.code: SELECT name, COALESCE(phone, 'No phone') AS contact_phone FROM customers;
worked_example.explanation: COALESCE returns the first non-null argument.

concepts.title: Sorting and limiting results
concepts.objective: Sort rows with ORDER BY ASC/DESC and truncate with LIMIT.

worked_example.title: ORDER BY and LIMIT
worked_example.code: SELECT product_name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5;
worked_example.explanation: Sorts descending by price and returns the top 5 most expensive products.

concepts.title: GROUP BY and summary aggregates
concepts.objective: Aggregate rows using COUNT, SUM, AVG, and GROUP BY.

worked_example.title: Department average salary
worked_example.code: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS headcount, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;
worked_example.explanation: GROUP BY collapses rows with identical department_id into summary rows.

concepts.title: Relational joins (INNER and LEFT)
concepts.objective: Combine related tables using explicit join predicates.

worked_example.title: INNER JOIN on foreign key
worked_example.code: SELECT o.id, c.customer_name, o.amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id;
worked_example.explanation: Matches rows where order customer_id equals customer primary key id.

concepts.title: Problem contracts, input bounds, and tracing
concepts.objective: Trace algorithm execution step-by-step and verify boundary behavior.

worked_example.title: Tracing loop invariants
worked_example.explanation: Before loop s=0; after element 1, s=1; after element 2, s=3; after 3, s=6.

concepts.title: Linear scanning and in-place manipulation
concepts.objective: Traverse arrays linearly, maintaining read and write pointers.

worked_example.title: Moving elements in a scan
worked_example.explanation: Separating read and write indices avoids allocating extra memory.

concepts.title: Hash maps and frequency counting
concepts.objective: Trade space for time by caching element occurrences in a hash map.

worked_example.title: Two-sum hash map lookup
worked_example.explanation: Looking up the complement in `seen` reduces time complexity from O(n^2) to O(n).

concepts.title: Two-pointer convergence and sorting
concepts.objective: Use converging pointers on sorted arrays to achieve optimal O(n) solutions.

worked_example.title: Pair sum on sorted array
worked_example.explanation: Adjusting either pointer deterministically moves the sum closer to target.

concepts.title: Numbers, operations and precedence
concepts.objective: Apply order of operations (BODMAS/PEMDAS) and signed arithmetic to calculations.

worked_example.title: Order of operations
worked_example.explanation: Brackets are evaluated first, then multiplication and division left-to-right, then addition.

concepts.title: Pattern recognition and classification
concepts.objective: Identify underlying rules in sequences and classify items based on stated constraints.

worked_example.title: Rule deduction
worked_example.code:
# Sequence: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30 ...
# Differences: +4, +6, +8, +10 -> Next difference is +12 -> 42.
worked_example.explanation: Analyzing differences between consecutive terms reveals a linear progression of +2.

concepts.title: Sentence structure and clause boundaries
concepts.objective: Identify subject, verb, and object components and avoid comma splices or run-on sentences.

worked_example.title: Subject-verb alignment
worked_example.code:
# Incorrect: 'The group of students were studying.'
# Correct: 'The group of students was studying.' (Subject is singular 'group')
worked_example.explanation: Prepositional phrases between the subject and verb do not alter subject number.

concepts.title: Functional vs non-functional requirements
concepts.objective: Distinguish feature capabilities (functional) from quality attributes like latency and uptime.

worked_example.title: Requirement categorization
worked_example.code:
# 'A user can upload an image' -> Functional requirement
# 'The image must be processed within 500ms' -> Non-functional (performance)
worked_example.explanation: Functional requirements define what the system does; non-functional define how well it performs.

concepts.title: AI, ML, and deep learning boundaries
concepts.objective: Understand the hierarchy between artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep neural nets.

worked_example.title: Rule-based vs Learning-based
worked_example.code:
# Rule-based: if email.contains('lottery') -> spam
# ML-based: model trained on 100k labeled emails learns token statistical weights
worked_example.explanation: Traditional software relies on explicit coded rules; machine learning learns parameters from data.

concepts.title: Structuring a technical self-introduction
concepts.objective: Deliver a concise 60-90 second introduction covering education, technical strengths, and recent projects.

worked_example.title: Present-Past-Future model
worked_example.code:
# 1. Present: Current status and core strengths (e.g. backend Python & SQL)
# 2. Past: Meaningful project built and deterministic test evidence
# 3. Future: Why this specific engineering role aligns with current growth
worked_example.explanation: A structured introduction stays focused, relevant, and under 90 seconds.
